sections.html:
Eastman, the biggest city, doubles as the Dodge County seat, in the middle of Georgia's southern half. Chauncey, Eastman and Milan are cities. Chester and Rhine are towns. Most sellers here have a rural or small-town parcel, and county offices in Eastman handle nearly every step of a sale.

The population was 19,663 in 2025, down 1.7% since April 2020. The county has 8,643 housing units, and builders took out just 5 permits in 2025. About 70.6% of homes are lived in by their owners, the middle home value is $118,100, and median gross rent is $723.

With prices this low, an unpaid tax balance or a missed exemption filing eats a larger share of what you net. Look up the parcel's tax status before listing.

sections.h2: Who to call about Dodge County property tax
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner is at 478-374-2154 and the Tax Assessors are at 478-374-8122. County government works out of 643 Pearl Bates Avenue in Eastman, and the clerk of courts answers at 478-374-2871.

Across Georgia the split is the same. The commissioner collects money and, in most counties, takes homestead filings. The assessors answer for the appraised value and for appeals. The county website has a Tax Payments link for paying online. The cities and towns inside the county have their own numbers:

  • Chauncey: 229-868-2296
  • Chester: 478-358-4550
  • Eastman: 478-374-7721
  • Milan: 229-362-4290
  • Rhine: 229-385-5521

If your house sits inside a city, ask both the county and the city clerk whether city tax comes on a separate bill.

sections.h2: Assessment notices and the appeal window
sections.html:
Assessment notices go out in the mail each summer. Your 45 days to appeal start on the mailing date, so jot that date down the day the envelope shows up. Miss it and that year's value stands until the next notice.

Appeals can be filed by email, by U.S. mail, or online through the appeal module on the qPublic site. If you did not receive a notice, or have a question about one, call the assessors at 478-374-8122.

The processing fee for conservation use (CUVA), forest land protection (FLPA) and other preferential parcels is $30.00 for new, renewal and continuation covenants. Owners of farm or timber land should ask the assessors whether a covenant is recorded on the parcel before listing.

The statewide appeal form asks you to choose one of three routes. File it with the Dodge County Board of Tax Assessors, because the state revenue office cannot change a local value.

Appeal tracks
TrackWhat it coversWhat happens next
Board of EqualizationDisputes over worth, uniform treatment, whether the property is taxable, or a turned-down exemptionAssessors can revise the notice themselves; otherwise a hearing is set and a ruling follows
Hearing officerWorth or uniformity of real property that is not a homestead and is valued above $500,000A ruling, then superior court if the dispute continues
ArbitrationValue onlyYou send in a certified appraisal within 45 days of the acknowledgment, and a hearing follows within 30 days
  • To take a ruling to superior court, send the assessors written notice inside 30 days of the decision
  • After an appeal is filed, the board sets up a settlement conference and sends notice inside 45 days
  • Superior court waits until you have paid the previous year's amount of tax
  • If the final value lands at 85 percent or less of the earlier figure, you can recover costs and attorney's fees

sections.h2: When Dodge County taxes are due
sections.html:
Unless the county picks something else, bills are due December 20. A county can choose December 1, November 15 or installments instead, and interest does not start until 60 days after the postmark on the bill. Go by the date printed on your Dodge bill, and call 478-374-2154 for a replacement if yours is lost.

Late balances can add penalties to the interest. Before closing, ask the tax commissioner for the amount your parcel owes, get it in writing, and hand a copy to the closing agent.

Returns of value are accepted from January 1 through April 1. Owners who paid last year and send nothing in are treated as repeating last year's final value, which is why most homeowners never file one.

Dodge County has no local homestead exemption beyond the statewide one. File once the house is your primary residence. To get the benefit in the first year, the application has to be in by April 1.

If you skip the application, you lose that year's exemption. The standard exemption knocks $2,000 off the assessed value, and assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value. Ask which office takes the form so you walk to the right window.

Refunds exist for tax assessed or collected in error, with a claim due inside three years of payment. Selling does not earn you a partial-year refund, because who owned the house on January 1 settles who owes the whole year.

sections.h2: Taxes at a Dodge County closing
sections.html:
Because liability sits with the January 1 owner, a fall closing still leaves you holding the whole year's bill. The purchase contract sets the split, and the settlement statement shows each side's share.

Two recorded items come up at closing. The buyer's long-term loan produces a security deed that has to be recorded in the county within 90 days, with an intangible tax that the superior court clerk usually collects. The sale itself triggers Georgia's transfer tax, which the seller owes and which is worked out from the price at the clerk's office. Any county tax lien sits on the general execution docket there, and that is where a title search finds it.

Listing land or a house outside town? Collect the papers buyers request first: the parcel record from qPublic, an answer from the assessors on any conservation or forest covenant, and a written balance from the tax commissioner.

A cash buyer can often close faster, but the title search still checks for liens on the general execution docket and for unpaid tax. Clearing those items first means nothing stalls the closing at the last minute. Keep copies of the payoff letter and the receipt with your closing papers.

Rural sales also turn on a few small details. Confirm the acreage and boundaries on the assessor's map against what your deed says. Find out if a mobile home or outbuilding shares the parcel and whether it was returned for tax. If the parcel lies inside Chauncey, Eastman, Milan, Chester or Rhine, add the city clerk to your list of calls so no second bill turns up after the sale.

faqs.q: Which number reaches Dodge County's tax office?
faqs.a: Call the Dodge County Tax Commissioner at 478-374-2154. The Tax Assessors, at 478-374-8122, answer questions about values and appeals.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Dodge County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the day the notice was mailed. Appeals can go in by email, U.S. mail, or the appeal module on the qPublic site.

faqs.q: Does Dodge County have its own homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. Only the statewide exemption applies, and owners request it through the county by April 1 of the first benefit year.

faqs.q: When are Dodge County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The state default is December 20 unless the county sets another date or installments. Owners also get 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest. Use the date printed on your bill.

faqs.q: Can I get property tax back after selling my Dodge County house?
faqs.a: Georgia law does not refund a partial year, because the January 1 owner is liable for all of it. A refund is available only for tax assessed or collected in error, with a claim within three years of payment.
